info.title: Tools — every layer
info.description: The call contracts of the harness's Tools, one operation per Tool, generated from the Tool nodes (`schemas/tools/tool.ts`) so standard API tooling can read them. **No HTTP server serves these paths**: each Tool is reached as its `x-invoke` says — a command line, an MCP tool, or an in-process call. Tags are the skills each Tool satisfies.

post.description: Assemble every declared `memory` directory's nodes into each agent's memory, per vendor: Claude Code's `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md` (a marked region, injected when the subagent starts) and Antigravity's workspace skill `.agents/skills/<agent>-memory/SKILL.md`. Other vendors (Gemini CLI, Copilot, Codex, Cursor) are not generated.

memory.description: Each agent's assembled memory file, per vendor.

post.summary: Check that an ArchiMate model's fhir-actor tags point at the IG's FHIR ActorDefinitions
post.description: Actors come first: the IG's ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK's personas, and an ArchiMate model only points at them. For one model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names, this reads every element carrying the Archi property `fhir-actor`, whose value is an ActorDefinition's canonical URL, and the IG's ActorDefinitions: FSH `InstanceOf: ActorDefinition` under `input/fsh/`, and FHIR JSON under `fsh-generated/resources/` or `input/resources/`, each canonical being `<sushi-config canonical>/ActorDefinition/<id>` unless its `url` says otherwise. It fails on a value that is not a canonical URL, a tag that names no ActorDefinition, an element kind that cannot be an actor (a data object, a goal), and a type mismatch (a `#person` actor on an application or technology element, a `#system` actor on a business actor or role). It warns about each ActorDefinition no element realizes; `--strict` makes that a failure. `--json` prints element → actors and actor → elements, for page back-links. It never writes an ActorDefinition or any FSH, and never matches boxes to actors by name.

instance.description: The layer root whose ArchiMate model is read.

model.description: The model's id from the config.

ig.description: The IG directory holding `sushi-config.yaml` and `input/fsh/`; absent, the layer root.

strict.description: Fail, not only warn, when an ActorDefinition is realized by no element of the model.

json.description: Print the back-links as JSON (element → actors, actor → elements, problems, unrealized) instead of the report.

report.description: The problems, the unrealized ActorDefinitions and a summary line; with `--json`, the back-links as JSON. Exit 1 on any problem, or on an unrealized actor under `--strict`.

x-selection.when: In an IG whose systems are drawn in an ArchiMate model, after its ActorDefinitions are written from the DAK personas: when model authors tag boxes `fhir-actor` in Archi, in CI, and before generating pages that link boxes to actors.
x-selection.limits: Reads one model per run. Checks pointers only: it never creates an ActorDefinition, and an actor missing from the IG is added there, by hand, from its persona. Reads FSH by pattern, not with SUSHI, so an ActorDefinition made only through a RuleSet is not seen until its JSON is generated.
x-selection.cost: One parse of the model and of the IG's FSH; milliseconds. No network, no JVM, no SUSHI.

post.summary: Draw a document's tables and figures from its ArchiMate data, and check the model against the document's relationship rules
post.description: For each table a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` lists under `tables`, rewrites the block's Markdown table from an `archimate-relationship-rules/v1` file (`relationship-rules`: source, relationship, target, note; `relationship-types`: picture, verb, meaning), keeping the caption and footnotes. For each figure under `figures` that names an `svg`, writes the view as SVG (the same drawing as the view's page). For a rules table that names a `model`, reports the rules the model never uses, the relationships no rule covers, the rules ArchiMate's relationship table refuses, and the relationship types the rules use without a meaning. The rules are in charge: nothing is rewritten from the model.

instance.description: The layer root whose config, models, rules and blocks are read.

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when a block or SVG is not what the data draws.

strict.description: Also exit 1 when the model has relationships no rule covers, or a rule is one ArchiMate does not allow.

blocks.description: The rewritten table blocks and figure SVGs, at the paths the config names; the rules check on stdout.

x-selection.when: When a document's table or figure restates an ArchiMate model (the element and relationship types it uses, the rules between them, a view): generate it instead of typing it, and run `--check` in CI so it cannot drift.
x-selection.limits: Draws relationship tables and view figures only; element-type tables and glossary tables are not covered yet. Checks a relationship's end types only, not derivation chains or viewpoints.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model named, one table lookup per relationship; milliseconds. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Check a layer's ArchiMate models against its config
post.description: The ArchiMate gate (graph typology `archimate`): every model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names is held, parses (Archi's native XML or its zipped archive), and resolves — every box in every view draws an element the model holds, every relationship's ends are in the model — and no `.archimate` file is held that the config does not name.

instance.description: The layer root whose `archimate` directory is checked.

problems.description: One line per problem on stderr, exit 1; or one ✓ line, exit 0.

x-selection.when: Before publishing a layer's ArchiMate models, and in its CI: a model that will not parse, draws an element it does not hold, or is held without being configured.
x-selection.limits: Archi's native format only; the Open Group exchange format is not read yet.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Count the tangles in ArchiMate views: lines crossing lines, and lines through boxes
post.description: For each view, as `render-view.ts` draws it, count the pairs of lines that cross and the lines that run through a box they do not connect (groups, and boxes that hold one of the line's ends, excepted). With `--view` it lists each tangle by the boxes it joins; with `--max` it is a gate.

model.description: The `.archimate` file (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive).

view.description: One view, by its Archi id (`id-<hex>`) or its page slug (e.g. `1-central-health-workforce-registry`). A slug, not free text, so no shell payload can ride on it. Absent: every view in the model.

max.description: Exit 1 if any view has more tangles than this.

json.description: Print JSON instead of one line per view.

tangles.description: Per view: crossings and lines through a box.

x-selection.when: Before and after every change to an ArchiMate view, so a change never adds tangles (skill `archimate-models`, "Untangle every view you touch").
x-selection.limits: Counts the lines as drawn by this harness's renderer, which draws a stale Archi route straight; Archi itself may draw the same view slightly differently.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per view. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Lower the tangles in ArchiMate views: re-route lines and swap same-size boxes in a row
post.description: Searches for a less tangled drawing of each view: a line may be re-routed straight or orthogonally (an L, or a Z through a free lane between boxes), and two same-size boxes in the same parent and row or column may swap places. A change is kept only if it lowers crossings + lines through boxes + lines drawn on top of each other. Without `--apply` it reports before and after per view; with it, the model is written back in place, only the moved boxes' bounds and the re-routed lines' bendpoints changing.

model.description: The `.archimate` file (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive).

view.description: One view, by its Archi id (`id-<hex>`) or its page slug (e.g. `1-central-health-workforce-registry`). A slug, not free text, so no shell payload can ride on it. Absent: every view in the model.

routes-only.description: Never move a box; only re-route lines.

apply.description: Write the model back in place.

json.description: Print JSON instead of one line per view.

report.description: Per view: tangles before and after, and the swaps and routes made.

x-selection.when: After drawing or changing an ArchiMate view, before committing it: run it, look at the drawing, keep what reads better (skill `archimate-models`).
x-selection.limits: A greedy search, one line or one swap at a time: it lowers tangles but does not find the best layout, never adds, resizes or regroups boxes, and leaves lines that end on lines, or share both ends with another line, as they are. The author still looks at the result.
x-selection.cost: Seconds for a large view (about 8 s for 20 views). No network, no JVM.

post.description: Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance's folio-glossary/v1 terms whose `focus` is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their `skosConcept` property (never by name) take the term's prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with `--prune` along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without `--write` it only reports; `--check` fails when anything would change. `--seed` goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under `library/` (`--from`): an authored model is never a source of the glossary.

instance.description: The instance root holding `glossary/*.glossary.json` and `archimate/cat-archimate.config.json`.

model.description: The model's id in the ArchiMate config. Required except with `--seed --from`.

write.description: Write the changes into the model file.

prune.description: Also remove relationships between linked elements that no term lists.

seed.description: Once: give linked terms without a focus the element type and relationships of an INGESTED model (under `library/`). Refused for an authored model.

from.description: With `--seed`: the ingested model file, under the instance's `library/`.

check.description: Fail if the model and the graph disagree.

model.description: The model file, rewritten in place with `--write`.

post.summary: Derive the metamodel an ArchiMate model uses, and check it against ArchiMate's relationship table
post.description: For each model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names: the element types it uses, with counts; every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern its relationships follow, with counts and ids; whether ArchiMate's relationship table (Appendix B of ArchiMate 3.2, as Archi holds it, committed as `archimate/schemas/archimate-relationships.json` in the tools layer) allows each pattern; and the placeholder elements, named after their own type, that a hand-drawn metamodel leaves in a model. Prints a report, JSON, Graphviz DOT or a Mermaid class diagram. `archimate-pages` draws the same result on each model's "Metamodel in use" page, so the metamodel is derived, never drawn.

instance.description: The layer root whose ArchiMate models are read.

model.description: One model's id from the config; absent, every model. Required for `--format dot` and `mmd`.

check.description: Exit 1 when any relationship follows a pattern ArchiMate does not allow. Placeholders are reported, never fatal.

metamodel.description: The report, or the metamodel as `archimate-metamodel/v1` JSON, DOT or Mermaid, on stdout.

x-selection.when: Before publishing an ArchiMate model (process `archimate-publish`, after `archimate-check`), in its CI, and whenever someone asks which element types and relationships a model actually uses — instead of drawing a metamodel view by hand.
x-selection.limits: Checks each relationship's type against its ends' types only; it does not check derivation chains, viewpoints or properties. A type the table does not know is reported as not checked, never as refused.
x-selection.cost: One parse per model and a table lookup per relationship; milliseconds. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Give every ArchiMate view, element and relationship a page and an IRI, and draw every view
post.description: Write a JSON-LD node and a thin page for each model a layer's `cat-archimate.config.json` names and for every view, element and relationship in it — keyed by Archi's own ids — plus the normalised model the pages' one loader draws from, and every view drawn as SVG from the model's own bounds and bendpoints in ArchiMate's notation, each box a link to its element. `--out` writes into a site being built — the data at the graph's path, the pages at the route of the visualiser the layer declares for this Tool, `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/`; without it the files go into the graph and `--check` gates them.

instance.description: The layer root.

out.description: A site being built: the data lands at `<out>/<graph path>/` and the pages at `<out>/<locale>/<harness>/<id>/`, the route of the layer's one visualiser `renderedBy` this Tool (none declared: nothing is written). Absent, they are written into the graph, which must be `served: true`.

check.description: Without `--out`: fail if a committed page is missing, stale or orphaned; write nothing.

pages.description: Pages and view drawings written (or found current).

x-selection.when: A folio's staging or publish build should show its ArchiMate models: run after the document site is built and before the navbar pass.
x-selection.limits: Draws the notation, not Archi's icons, custom images or fonts; sketch and canvas views are skipped. Never replaced by Archi's CLI report (skill `archimate-models`).
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per view; four models of 5,809 pages and 131 drawings (~24 MB) take about 1.5 s. No network, no JVM.

post.summary: Figure redrawn as drawn, from its PDF vector layer
post.description: Draw a figure as SVG from `as-drawn-figure/v1` data: the drawing `scripts/pdf-as-drawn.py` transcribes from the source PDF's vector layer (every path, clip, text run and image in the L1 figure region, at its printed position, colour and size). The SVG keeps the original's layout and style; labels are SVG text held to their printed width, and labels that name a glossary concept link to it.

data.description: An as-drawn-figure/v1 file, or a directory of them.

check.description: Write nothing; fail when data is invalid or an SVG is stale.

svg.description: One SVG per data file, named after the figure labels it draws.

x-selection.when: A folio's L1 figure has no model route (ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, FHIR, a figure-data family) or needs an as-drawn companion to its model view, and should be an SVG that looks like the printed figure rather than a PNG crop.
x-selection.limits: Transcribes; does not interpret. Soft-masked paints (drop shadows) are left out and counted in `omitted`. Fonts fall back to Source Sans or Arial, held to the printed width.
x-selection.cost: Reads JSON files; no network.

post.description: Render index pages for the declared skills, docs and swimlane-glossary directories, one per directory.

check.description: Fail if a page is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under the harness's own site directory. A repository's own site build passes it (the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts`), since its harness docs are a pinned mount.

scope.description: A scoped site build: the comma-separated instances whose pages this writer writes (the IG and the layer it lands on); every other instance's pages are linked on that layer's own site. Passed by the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts` (owner, 2026-11-08, Q-SZ-2 "B"). Absent: every instance.

pages.description: The viewer pages, under the published site directory.

post.description: Render the declared avatar nodes — an actor's glyph and colours, including the overlay states — into the stylesheet the site serves.

check.description: Compare against the committed copy and fail if stale, instead of writing.

post.description: Render every reference in the checkout (each declared `references` directory's folio-reference/v1 nodes and each `catalogue` directory's Dublin Core records) as the bibliography page and one page per sub-graph, each with its BibTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS and Dublin Core JSON-LD exports and a per-reference export, at the route of the visualiser core declares for it.

check.description: Fail if a page or export is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under cat-harness's docs, as a repository's own site build does (`visualiser-writers.ts`).

scope.description: A scoped site build: the comma-separated instances whose pages this writer writes (the IG and the layer it lands on); every other instance's pages are linked on that layer's own site. Passed by the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts` (owner, 2026-11-08, Q-SZ-2 "B"). Absent: every instance.

pages.description: The bibliography pages and their exports, under the published site directory.

post.description: Each labelled block's links back to where it can be changed: [edit] opens the block's Markdown source in GitHub's editor on `main`, and [feedback] opens a new GitHub issue about the block, from the folio's `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/block-feedback.yml` when it has one (prefilling only the fields it declares: block, section, source, page, url) or as a plain issue whose body carries the same facts. The document build draws these on every block; this Tool prints them as JSON for one block or all. Governed by the `block-actions` skill.

repo.description: The folio's repository root. Default: the working directory.

block.description: One block's label. Absent: every block of every document. A label no block has exits 1.

github.description: `owner/name` on GitHub. Default `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else the checkout's `origin`. None at all exits 2: no links rather than broken ones.

issue-template.description: The issue form's file name under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. Default `block-feedback.yml`, used only if the folio has it.

links.description: JSON on stdout: one `{ label, source, section, edit, feedback }` per block. A one-line summary goes to stderr.

x-selection.when: A reader, reviewer or agent wants to propose a change to, or give feedback on, one block of a document folio, and needs the link that lands on that block rather than on the repository.
x-selection.limits: Builds URLs; it writes nothing to GitHub. Only labelled blocks get links. The issue form's fields are read by a line scan for `id:`, so a form must declare its ids plainly.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds: one walk of the document manifests. No network.

post.description: Generate, per diagram, a checklist that walks the BPMN as a state machine: each task names the `workflow_complete` call that records it and ends with `next:` by node id; each decision lists its labelled branches (or the DMN that computes it); parallel forks name every branch and joins wait for all; start/end events are entry and exit lines. A rendering, never an authority: it says it is generated, and `--check` fails when one is stale.

out.description: Write every `<stem>.checklist.md` into this one directory instead. Default: each beside its diagram, in the layer that owns it; the harness site's `assets/workflows/checklists` holds those of the layers below the harness.

check.description: Verify instead of write: exit 1 on a stale, missing or orphaned checklist.

checklists.description: One committed `<stem>.checklist.md` per diagram in every layer, beside its `.bpmn`.

x-selection.when: A coding agent needs a process in a form it can follow without reading BPMN XML, or without the engine's MCP server.
x-selection.limits: Conditions are the flows' labels or the DMN's id; a condition expression the model does not carry is not reproduced. The engine stays the authority.
x-selection.cost: One diagram load per process; no network.

post.description: Run a declared BPMN process as an instance: `workflow_start` opens one for a subject, `workflow_next` reports what is enabled, `workflow_complete` records a step or answers a decision (a DMN-computed one from `facts`) and REFUSES a step that is not enabled. State is committed under the work plan, so which edge was taken is a record, not a memory.

process.description: The process to run: a diagram's file stem or its `bpmn:process` id.

node.description: The step or decision to complete, as `workflow_next` reported it.

enabled.description: What may be worked next, after each call.

x-selection.when: Work follows a declared process and its order must be enforced and recorded: a step done out of order should be refused, not just discouraged.
x-selection.limits: Reached over MCP; an agent without the server can walk the generated checklist (`bpmn-checklist`) by hand, but nothing then refuses a wrong turn.
x-selection.cost: One diagram load per call; state is a small committed file.

post.description: Render each process diagram to SVG for the documentation site. The .bpmn file is the source of truth; the picture is generated from it, so a diagram and its image cannot disagree.

check.description: Fail if any committed SVG is stale, instead of writing.

diagrams.description: The generated SVG directory. Never hand-edited.

post.summary: Build, check and (on request) publish a layer's own site, or a branches/<branch> preview
post.description: From a checkout whose layers arrive by remote mount: mount the pinned closure, install, run the layer's own gates (`--pre`), compose the harness chrome for THIS layer, run its source steps, build with Jekyll at the base path read from the git remote (`/<repo>`, or `/<repo>/branches/<branch>` for a preview), run the post-build steps (mount-instance-docs, pdf-viewer, set-html-lang, publish-id-lookup, rail-standalone-pages), and check that every relative or base-rooted link in every page resolves to a file under the site, reading each page with an HTML parser. Any failing step stops the run; a link that does not resolve means nothing is published. It never decides to publish: only `--publish` does, and then a root publish keeps `branches/` and `_render-log/` on the branch, and a preview replaces only its own `branches/<branch>/`.

root.description: The layer checkout (holds `index.config.json`). Default: the working directory.

instance.description: The declared layer name; must match the checkout's declaration.

home.description: A page that becomes the site's index.md.

pre.description: A package script to run in the checkout first, as `bun run <name>` (repeatable): the layer's own gates. Any non-zero exit stops the build.

sourceStep.description: A package script that writes into the site source, run as `bun run <name> <site source>` (repeatable).

siteStep.description: A package script that writes finished pages into the BUILT site, run as `bun run <name> <built site>` after Jekyll (repeatable): Jekyll drops `_`-prefixed directories, so a generator whose pages sit under one runs here.

staging.description: Build (and with --publish, publish) a preview of this branch at branches/<branch>/.

noMount.description: Use the mounts already on disk.

publish.description: Publish after every check passes; needs --remote.

remote.description: The https git URL the caller can push the pages branch to.

site.description: The built site directory, and its base path.

links.description: Pages checked, unresolved links (must be 0), files.

x-selection.when: Publishing a layer's site, or a branch preview of it, from an agent or a Routine: the agent-run replacement for a pages workflow.
x-selection.limits: Layer sites only. A FHIR IG's site (the IG pipeline layer's `stage-ig-sites`) is not built here yet; it needs the IG's FHIR packages, which some environments cannot reach.
x-selection.cost: A full mount, install and Jekyll build: minutes, not seconds. `--no-mount` reuses what is on disk.

post.summary: Rank candidate glossary terms in prose by C-value
post.description: The scoring step of the `automatic-term-extraction` method: count the word n-grams of one or more Markdown or text files (not across punctuation, front matter or code), and rank them by C-value as Frantzi & Ananiadou 1996 define it, so nested multi-word terms are not swamped by the longer phrases that contain them. Tested against the paper's own worked example (Table 2). Every row is a candidate; it writes nothing and promotes nothing.

files.description: One or more Markdown or text files whose prose is read.

maxLength.description: Longest n-gram, in words; 1 or more. Default 5.

minFreq.description: Fewest occurrences an n-gram needs to be scored. Default 3, the paper's cut-off; 1 or more.

top.description: How many candidates to print; 1 or more. Default 50.

edgeStopwords.description: Drop n-grams that begin or end with a common English function word. Off by default, because the 1996 method has no such filter.

json.description: Print the candidates as JSON, each with its frequency, nesting counts and C-value.

candidates.description: A ranked table, or JSON with `status: candidate`, of n-grams with a C-value above 0.

x-selection.when: A person or agent wants candidate glossary terms from a body of prose, ranked, to review before writing any definitions.
x-selection.limits: Statistics only, as the 1996 paper: no part-of-speech filter (the later C-value papers that add one are not held), English word splitting, and no reference corpus. On ordinary prose without --edge-stopwords the top rows are function phrases. A person decides what is a term.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds for a chapter; linear in words times --max-length. No network.

post.description: The zod definition of `<name>.json` — what a layer may declare about itself — and the published JSON Schema generated from it.

baseUrl.description: Publication base; a preview passes its own.

post.summary: Catalogue a library from its bibliography
post.description: Write one `folio-dublin-core/v1` record and one `folio-catalogue-node/v1` item per library entry that the source ledger joins to a CSL-JSON reference, into the folio's declared `catalogue` directory, so `gen-library-jsonld` reads the title from the catalogue's `dc.title` instead of falling to the PDF or the slug. The join is exact: a ledger row naming the entry's `structure.json` source file, one reference id, and the same sha256 where both record one. Unjoined entries are reported and left alone. Never touches a node it did not write.

instance.description: The folio instance's root. It must declare a `catalogue` and a `library` directory.

apply.description: Write the records and nodes, and remove this tool's stale ones. Without it the run is a dry run.

check.description: Write nothing. Exit 1 if any record or node on disk differs from what the bibliography gives.

baseUrl.description: Where the bibliography is published. With `--apply`, writes `catalogue.json` when the catalogue directory has none; without it such a run is refused.

catalogue.description: `<catalogue>/records/<slug>.dc.json` and `<catalogue>/nodes/item-<slug>.json` per joined entry; `catalogue.json` when absent and `--base-url` is given. A summary of joined and left-alone entries goes to stdout.

x-selection.when: A folio keeps its bibliography as CSL-JSON and a source ledger, has no catalogue, and its library titles fall to `slug` or the PDF.
x-selection.limits: Bibliographic layer only. Every publication gate is written `unknown`: it records what the bibliography says and decides no licence. Entries the ledger does not join to exactly one reference are left alone, never guessed.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per entry. Reads the bibliography, the ledger and each entry's structure.json; no network.

post.description: Report which of the harness's optional and required dependencies are present on this machine, and what each unmet one blocks.

required_only.description: Report only the dependencies without which the harness cannot run.

report.description: Per-dependency: present, absent, or could not be determined.

post.summary: Verify Data Sharing Agreement hash, citation, and vocabulary terms
post.description: Verify a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) directory or single version: checks that every JSON-LD term in `agreement.jsonld` and `dcat.jsonld` is defined in the SHA-256-pinned official W3C ODRL 2.2, W3C DCAT 3 (with SPDX 2.2.2 and ADMS), or DCMI Metadata Terms contexts; checks that the ODRL 2.2 Agreement's `uid` is the version's fixed-version URL and its `dcterms:source` cites the DCAT 3 `dcat:Distribution` whose `spdx:checksum` is checked; verifies that the SHA-256 digest of `agreement.md` matches `spdx:checksumValue`; and checks `dcat:previousVersion` and hash distinctness across versions.

dir.description: Path to a versioned DSA directory (holding `v1/`, `v2/`, ...) or a single version directory holding `agreement.md`, `dcat.jsonld`, and `agreement.jsonld`. Defaults to `folio-assistant-core/scripts/test-fixtures/dsa`.

verdict.description: Per-version verification line (`dcat:version`, `dcat:downloadURL`, `sha256`) on stdout when valid; diagnostic findings on stderr with exit code 1 when any check fails.

x-selection.when: Verifying a Data Sharing Agreement's checksum, ODRL citation, DCAT 3 record and `dcat:previousVersion` chain, or `adms:status`.
x-selection.limits: Checks structural, cryptographic, and vocabulary conformance of `agreement.md`, `dcat.jsonld`, and `agreement.jsonld`; does not evaluate legal prose semantics or sign Verifiable Credentials.
x-selection.cost: Local file reads and SHA-256 hashing; runs in milliseconds with no network access.

post.summary: Do the Tool nodes agree with their skills?
post.description: Check every Tool node's joins: that each `satisfies` resolves to a real skill and agrees with that skill's declared contract, that every io port names a declared type, and that no argv input has a type able to express a shell payload.

report.description: The satisfies map, the count of skills with and without a Tool, then the verdict. Exit 0 every join holds, 1 at least one does not. A skill with NO Tool is reported and is NOT a failure: many skills are pure judgement, and failing on them would make the report unusable.

x-selection.when: Before pushing any change to `tools/`, and as the first of the three audits `code-node-review` lists. It is the check that refuses a contract nobody could satisfy.

post.summary: Is CI passing on the default branch?
post.description: Report each workflow's state on the default branch, which a checkout cannot see: a red workflow looks exactly like a green one from in here. One API call over the recent run history, not one request per workflow, so it stays inside the unauthenticated 60/hr limit and stays usable at session start.

markdown.description: Emit the block the session-start sweep prints. ALWAYS exits 0: the sweep runs it as `if ! …; then`, and a non-zero exit would print the report AND declare it unchecked every time CI is red.

out.description: Write the markdown report to a file AND keep the exit code — which `--markdown` cannot do, since it always exits 0. Its own flag, so one API call is not spent twice.

report.description: One row per workflow. Five verdicts, not two: green, red, `running`, `superseded` (a red whose workflow file changed after the failing run, so the verdict is against code that no longer exists), and possibly-stale (a red that has not re-run in a week). Three exit codes carry them to a caller that reads no rows: 0 nothing is red, 1 something is, 2 COULD NOT LOOK — the API was unreachable, or `--out` could not be written. A caller must never read 2 as either verdict. `--markdown` and `--warn` always exit 0 by design, so a caller wanting the verdict uses neither.

A finding in a control field, or any field the strict schema does not declare, is REFUSED, so a report cannot extend the delegator's plan. A finding in a data field is QUARANTINED: the original is kept and marked, never stripped. The patterns are a deterministic tripwire (instruction overrides, role and turn spoofs, fence breaks, tool-call syntax, hidden Unicode, exfiltration links, pipe-to-shell), a mitigation and not a guarantee. x-selection.cost: About 6 seconds for 11 harnesses. Nothing to install, no network.

post.summary: Build and publish an IG repository's own site with its folio-site.yml workflow
post.description: Dispatch the IG repository's `folio-site.yml` (copied from the IG layer's `ig-repo-site` template): on a runner it composes the harness chrome for THIS layer (`compose-docs --shell --instance`, `gen-navbar-include`), composes the IG at the root of that Jekyll shell (`stage-ig-sites --compose-at-root`), builds it with Jekyll so every IG page wears the theme's side bar, search box and icon row, publishes the layer's served directories, rails any page Jekyll did not lay out (`rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance`), stamps the platform that built it (`folio-build.json`), and on the default branch deploys the whole site to the `gh-pages` root. It reports platform drift against sibling sites and re-dispatches the IGs this one depends on when a token allows.

repo.description: The IG repository whose workflow to dispatch. Default: the current repository.

ref.description: The branch to build. Only the default branch deploys; any other builds and reports.

status.description: The dispatch, and the run it starts; the site is served once that run and GitHub's Pages deploy have finished.

It builds the IG with `stage-ig-sites`, not the IG's own `ghbuild.yml`, and has no plan or dry-run: a run on the default branch deploys. The agent pipeline does not use it.
x-selection.cost: One runner job, 8 to 15 minutes, plus GitHub's Pages deploy.

post.summary: Convert a checkout to a root index.config.json
post.description: Write the root `index.config.json` (`folio-index-config/v1`) that says which layers the checkout instantiates, where each comes from (`source.local` or `source.remote`) and which owns `/` (`site.landing`), from the root `*.config.json` files and the declaration's `remoteMounts`. With `--write` it moves `remoteMounts` off the declaration into `source.remote` entries, writes the generated `.gitignore` block, and renames a legacy `<name>.mount-lock.json` to `index.lock.json`. Without a flag it prints the index it would write. Idempotent: a re-run merges what the declaration gained, and refuses an entry the index already holds differently. A root config naming no layer is reported as `unmatched-config` and not imported, because what to do with it is a person's decision.

root.description: The checkout to convert; omitted, this one.

write.description: Write the index, move the mounts, write the ignore block and rename the lock.

check.description: Exit 1 when --write would change anything; write nothing.

findings.description: The index it would write or wrote, and each finding (`unmatched-config`, `unreadable-config`, `landing-undetermined`). Exit 0 written, up to date or planned; 1 stale under --check; 2 could not convert.

post.summary: Ingest, with PDF and image extensions
post.description: Ingest a PDF into `library/` — embedded outline, page text, OCR for scans, and image extraction — using PyMuPDF, tesseract and pypdf with Pillow.

file.description: The PDF to ingest, under the declared `uploads` graph.

x-selection.when: Reach for this when the upload is a PDF and you need its CONTENT — an outline-bearing document read at chapter granularity, a text-layer document read at page granularity, or a scan that must be OCR'd first. Confirm the backend is present before relying on it: `bun run cat check-deps`, or simply run the pair's entry point, which reports `no PDF backend` rather than guessing.
x-selection.limits: It adds nothing for archives, spreadsheets or metadata — `ingest-stdlib` does those, and does them where this cannot run. Its PDF rungs are tested in CI, which installs the lean set; the table rung (`pdf-tables.py`, camelot) is not, so anything gated on it is a path CI cannot exercise.
x-selection.cost: The lean set is 144 MB and CI installs it. `camelot-py` for `pdf-tables.py` is the part CI skips — 912 KB itself, but 323 MB with numpy, pandas and OpenCV, more than the whole lean set. The dependencies are not independent either: `pypdf` image extraction needs `Pillow`, and `cryptography` panics under pyo3 on IMPORT when `cffi` is missing. All of it is declared in `schemas/sdlc/python-deps.ts`, so the cost is read rather than rediscovered.

post.description: Ingest an upload into `library/` using only the Python standard library — archive listings, CSV and spreadsheet records, technical file metadata, and the content sniff that routes a file to its rung.

file.description: The upload to ingest, under the declared `uploads` graph.

outdir.description: Library root; defaults to the declared `library` graph.

dryRun.description: Report the chosen rung and stop.

x-selection.when: Reach for this first, and in CI always. It is the only one of the pair that runs where nothing has been installed — which is every fresh container and every CI job here, since the workflow installs `ruff` and nothing else. It covers archives, CSV and spreadsheets, technical metadata, and the sniff that decides which rung a file takes, including the OOXML/ODF container check that stops a workbook being listed as a bag of XML parts.
x-selection.limits: It cannot read a PDF. Text layer, embedded outline, page rendering, OCR and image extraction all need a backend it deliberately does not have, so a PDF routes to `undetermined` and is REFUSED rather than half-ingested. `ingest-extended` is the sibling that does those.
x-selection.cost: None beyond `python3` itself. No wheels, no C toolchain, no network, nothing to keep current, and no CI minutes spent installing.

post.summary: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
post.description: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness's declaration at its pin and every `needs`, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless --repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch's tip unless --pin says otherwise, its declaration's name checked), seeds them all into the repository's index.config.json with the consent given (`remote-mount --seed --whole`), sets `site.landing` to the harness, `site.agentRun` and `mountApprovers`, mounts the closure (`remote-mount`: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (`.github/cat.ts` and `.github/mount-from-lock.sh` from cat-harness-tools `templates/root-bootstrap/`) and sets the root's `cat` script to `bun .github/cat.ts`, so `bun run cat …` mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness's `instantiate:<harness>` checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/<harness>). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:<harness>` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches/<branch>/ (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin <name>=<sha>` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of <name>=<owner/repo>` says where a need lives.

repo.description: The checkout to harness: clean, with a GitHub origin. Default: the working directory.

harness.description: The harness, OWNER/REPO, pinned at its default branch's tip (pin it otherwise with --pin <name>=<sha>).

consentBy.description: Who consented to mounting the closure; also recorded as the one mountApprover. The evidence (where they consented, readable) is read from stdin.

evidence.description: Where the consent was given, readable (a session, an issue comment). On stdin because it is free prose: it quotes what was said.

branch.description: The setup branch. Default: harness/<harness>. Never the default branch.

plan.description: Resolve the closure, print every step, and stop.

local.description: Commit on the branch, push nothing; the site is built and composed (stage-local --dry-run).

noPr.description: Push the branch and the preview, open no PR.

url.description: The branch's preview, gh-pages branches/<branch>/, once GitHub's Pages deploy has run.

x-selection.when: A repository that mounts no harness yet is to be harnessed: an existing FHIR IG adopting a FHIR harness, a repository becoming a folio overlay. Its PR is the setup-only PR repo-conversion §4 asks for before any content PR.
x-selection.limits: The harness's own adoption steps are its checkout scripts instantiate:<harness> and prepare:<harness>; a harness that declares neither is mounted and rendered with what its layers already declare, and a site that needs a build input nobody produced (an IG with no AST) is refused by the render step with its reason. Re-pinning an already harnessed repository is remote-mount --seed, not this.
x-selection.cost: The mount: a blobless fetch of each layer of the closure and one install (a few minutes). Then the harness's prepare step (an IG's AST: a full IG Publisher run) and the render.

post.summary: Every reference a journey or a workshop names resolves
post.description: Read every `user-scenario` and `workshop` node in the checkout through the layers' declared directories, with the journeys viewer's own resolver, and resolve what each names: actors (`personas`, a step's `lead`, `experiences[].actor`, `handoff.from`/`to`, `illustrationStyle.cast[].actor`), user stories, `realisedBy` BPMN files (instance-relative) and the element ids in them, `uses` blocks in a directory declaring `building-blocks`, `req:` requirements, FHIR examples and a step's `dak` assets (data sets, decision tables, indicators) in a `fhir-artifact-index` (could not determine while the index is built at publish), `illustration.src` files, `follows`/`partOf`/`parts`/`includes` journeys (parts and includes forming no cycle; an `includes` held against the call activity its step's `realisedBy` names, could not determine when the call names no process), the `trustLadder` code list and each `record.state` code of it, and ArchiMate `views`; and each workshop's `scenarios`, `steps[]` `{scenario, step}` and `<scenario>#<step>` refs; each device screen's `owner` and `personCard` actors, its `steps[]` `{scenario, step}`, and the FHIR examples its `qr` and `recordList` blocks name; and every persona's `avatar` image path. Every journey is a DAK user scenario (the kind `specialises` it): its DAK personas, the roles its persona actors play, must be non-empty and each a declared role; a persona may be an actor or (0.4.0) a role. What is derived is not also written: a listed part's `follows` or `partOf`, personas equal to the parts', a lead equal to the lanes' first actor, are each a redundant finding, and a 0.4.0 step with no experiences whose lanes no persona plays is a finding. A node that does not parse is a finding. One line per finding, naming the layer, file and step. Exit 0 every reference resolves (or no layer holds a journey or a workshop, which is said); 1 one does not; 2 the declarations could not be read.

root.description: A directory in the checkout to check. Default: the working directory.

findings.description: Unresolved references and unparsed nodes, one line each on stderr, with the count of references examined; or one ✓ line.

x-selection.when: In every layer pull request's checks (it is a `check:` script, so the gate set derives it), and before publishing a site whose layer declares a `journeys-viewer` visualiser: a journey that names a story, a BPMN task, a block or an image that is not there.
x-selection.limits: A `realisedBy` process and an `illustration.src` are resolved in the journey's own layer only, as the viewer draws them; the other references are looked up in the journey's layer first, then in every layer the checkout mounts.
x-selection.cost: One read of the checkout's declared directories, as the viewer makes; milliseconds per journey.

post.description: Draw every journey (`user-scenario`) and workshop (`workshop`) in the checkout as static pages at the route of the visualiser a layer declares for this Tool, `<locale>/<instance>/<id>/`: an index of all journeys, grouped by layer (each a sub-graph page), each parent's `parts` nested under it in its order with optional and repeating parts marked (an older file's `partOf` children after them, ordered along `follows`), and a plain DAK user scenario with no steps listed as one; one page per journey, its parts in order and the journeys it is a part of, a journey map with a lane and a feeling curve per persona, then each step, linked to the journey it `includes`, with its BPMN drawing (the step's flow nodes highlighted), user stories, requirements, FHIR examples, building blocks, the DAK assets it uses (data sets, decision tables and indicators, linked into the IG) and ArchiMate views; and the workshop layer, the questions for the room on each step, a page per workshop and per module, job aids, and printable A3/A4 sheets; and each device screen (`device-screen`) that shows a step a workshop presents, drawn as a static device mock (phone, tablet, scanner, desktop, kiosk) with its owner beside it, in the workshop's Device Demo, linked both ways with the walkthrough. A persona's picture (`meta.persona.avatar`) is drawn wherever the persona appears. Layers below the declaring one are read through their declarations, so a downstream site shows the journeys of the layers it mounts too.

instance.description: The layer whose `visualisers` declare this Tool: the pages go to that visualiser's route. One that declares none gets nothing, and the run exits 78 (not applicable).

site.description: A site being built: the pages are written at the declared route under it. Absent, under the layer's own site directory. The route is this Tool's alone and is replaced whole.

pages.description: The viewer's pages and its two assets (`assets/journeys.css`, `assets/journeys.js`), under the declared route.

x-selection.when: A site build of a layer that declares a `journeys-viewer` visualiser over its `user-scenario`, `workshop` and `device-screen` directories; run with the other declared writers (`visualiser-writers.ts`), before the navbar pass.
x-selection.limits: Static pages: the stepper, the filter and the remembered assessment ticks are a small dependency-free script, and every page reads complete without it. A FHIR example links to its page only where a layer declares a `fhir-artifact-index`; an ArchiMate view is drawn only where its layer declares `archimate-pages`. A device screen is drawn in the one state its node says: a toggle is drawn on or off, a button is a label; a workshop that declares no screen for its steps frames its own app (`presentation.deviceDemo`) instead.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds per journey; a BPMN drawing is inlined once per step that names it.

post.description: Audit every join in the actor→role→skill→task sentence and write a committed QA sidecar per node. The sidecar distinguishes "unbound since it was drawn" from "broken in the commit under review".

check.description: Compare against the committed sidecars and fail on a critical finding or a stale one, instead of writing.

strict.description: Promote `major` to failing as well. Not what CI runs; see the note on constant-red checks in `remote-skill-servable.test.ts`.

worstSeverity.description: critical, major, minor — or none. `unknown` findings are never a pass.

post.description: Dump this layer's knowledge graph — skills, BPMN activities and their lanes, roles, actors, directories — to one JSON-LD document for publication. The export is data; something else draws it.

baseUrl.description: Publication base the node IRIs are minted against; a preview passes its own.

problems.description: Sources that could not be read, counted rather than silently omitted.

post.summary: Retrieve a remote Knowledge Graph via npm package or tarball
post.description: Retrieve and inspect a remote Knowledge Graph packaged as an npm package or tarball (.tgz), supporting both unhydrated source graph views (authored declarations, skills, schemas) and hydrated materialized graph views (subgraph JSON-LD, metadata indexes, dereferenced graph projections).

package.description: Package name, npm tarball (.tgz) path, or URL.

destination.description: Directory to unpack or install into.

view.description: Graph view to inspect/retrieve: 'unhydrated' (source graph), 'hydrated' (materialized JSON-LD/indexes), or 'both'.

release.description: Optional `folio-binary-release/v1` record to verify digest and size against.

summary.description: Summary of retrieved graphs, nodes, and assets.

post.summary: Validate a node in the graph
post.description: Check one file against the schema for its graph typology. ONE tool for every schema: the kind is resolved from the declared directory that holds the file.

path.description: The node to check. Its graph typology is resolved from the declared directory that contains it.

lenient.description: Accept partial coverage knowingly: downgrade could-not-determine from an error to a warning.

report.description: One line per file — valid, invalid with the failing paths, or could-not-determine with the reason. Exit 0 valid, 1 invalid or undetermined, 2 misuse.

x-selection.when: Whenever a node's shape matters and you are not in this repository's CI: `tools/` is an INHERITED declaration and `.github/workflows/` is not, so a downstream layer gets this and none of the CI gates.

post.description: Render the layer's published knowledge graph as one page: facets by kind and sub-graph, search, a node's properties, its edges and back-links, and the graph's own gaps — reading the JSON-LD document at the site root rather than carrying a copy.

check.description: Fail if a page is stale, instead of writing.

site.description: A site being built: write the pages at their declared route under it instead of under the harness's own site directory. A repository's own site build passes it (the tools layer's `visualiser-writers.ts`), since its harness docs are a pinned mount.

pages.description: The viewer pages, under the published site directory.

post.description: Is a `library/<bib-slug>/` entry complete as L1 source content? Each requirement is met, unmet, or NOT-DERIVABLE.

targetPath.description: One `library/<bib-slug>/` entry. Absent, every entry the declared `library` graph holds.

report.description: Per requirement: met, unmet, or `not-derivable` — the third distinguishes a document that CANNOT yield an artefact from one that simply has not. Exit 2 means no `library` graph is declared anywhere, which the script states as "This is NOT a pass. Treat it as unknown."

post.description: Of the normative sentences in a publication (the closed marker list of the methodology `l1-coverage` §1), count how many an L1 extraction CAPTURED, how many are EXCLUDED for a fixed-list reason a person signed off, and how many are UNACCOUNTED — per page and in total. Writes the contract's §4 report and exits non-zero below 100% accounted-for.

text.description: The publication's body text, page-tagged: `{"pages":[{"page":n,"text":"…"}]}` JSON, or plain text with a form feed between pages (what `pdftotext` writes). Headers, references and tables of contents are stripped by the caller.

captured.description: JSON `[{"id","text"}]`: every statement the extraction captured, verbatim.

exclusions.description: JSON `[{location|text, reason, signedOffBy?, signedOffAt?}]`. An exclusion without `signedOffBy` is a proposal and leaves its sentence unaccounted.

out.description: Where to write the report; stdout when absent.

report.description: An `l1-coverage-report/v1` JSON report: definitionVersion, matchMethod, source and graph sha256, totals, pages[] and sentences[]. A per-page table goes to stderr.

x-selection.when: An L1 extraction of a publication (recommendations, remarks, schedule entries) is about to be reviewed or promoted, and somebody needs to know — rather than assume — that no normative sentence was silently missed.
x-selection.limits: Matching is normalised substring, so a paraphrased capture reads as unaccounted. Body-text filtering is the caller's. The marker list is English.
x-selection.cost: Reads three files; no network.

post.description: Compile a rendered paper's `main.tex` with latexmk inside a TeX Live (full) image, for a host with Docker but no TeX engine. pdf.description: The compiled PDF beside the input.

post.description: Turn a pdflatex log's Overfull \hbox warnings into a located, actionable report, with a threshold so a long tail of trivial overruns does not bury the real ones.

warn.description: Report without failing — for a corpus not yet clean.

findings.description: Compile-breaking hazards, located. A clean run here is not a successful compile; it is the absence of these classes.

post.description: Compile LaTeX source documents into PDF using latexmk with safe shell-escape isolation across CI events.

tex.description: The TeX source file to compile (e.g. main.tex).

args.description: Additional arguments to forward to latexmk.

post.description: Inspect Lean declarations chapter by chapter for proofs that type-check, are sorry-free and axiom-clean, and still carry no mathematical content — assuming what they claim, concluding something trivially true, or resting on a false premise.

chapter.description: One chapter instead of the whole corpus.

checkAxioms.description: Axiom-cleanliness is a separate question from vacuity: a proof can be axiom-clean and still assume its conclusion.

findings.description: Sorry inventory and trivial-truth detections. Sibling of `lean-coverage`, not an alternative to it: that one COUNTS what is proved, this one asks whether a proof says anything.

post.description: Build every Lean project in the workspace from the root Lake manifest, so cross-package dependencies resolve against it rather than a possibly-stale per-paper manifest. Writes a committable build-status sidecar every run.

paper.description: Build one paper instead of all of them.

cache.description: Fetch the Mathlib cache first. A from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes against ~2 for a restore.

logDir.description: Where logs and the status sidecar go.

status.description: `lean-build-status.json` — committable, so a green build is distinguishable from one nobody ran.

post.description: Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt `.lake/` artefacts for a Lean package. Always try `restore` first: a from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes, a restore about two.

action.description: The verb. `doctor` tells a restore that silently missed from one that worked.

lakeRoot.description: The package whose `.lake/` is acted on.

result.description: A real hit, a miss, or a diagnosis — never a miss that reads as a hit.

post.description: Count how many provable blocks — theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary — carry a full Lean proof rather than a sorry, per paper. The completeness half of the Lean audit: what is formalised, and what is still a gap.

contentRoot.description: Where content blocks live. not a Lean project root.

coverage.description: Provable blocks, and how many are sorry-free. A count, not a verdict: a sorry-free proof can still be vacuous, which is the sibling node's question.

post.summary: Formal edges from the Lean build
post.description: Extract ELABORATED formal dependencies between a folio's lean.ref declarations (LeanArchitect's rule over the folio's own lean.ref set). Needs a Lean toolchain and a built Lake project. Tagged declarations missing from the build are reported, never recorded as dependency-free; with ingest the result is recorded in the formal cache as source "elaborated".

lake_dir.description: The folio's Lake project directory (holds lakefile.* and .lake/).

root.description: Content root to collect lean.ref targets from (default: the folio's declared one).

ingest.description: Record the result in the formal cache as source "elaborated".

report.description: The extracted edges, or why they could not be determined — never an empty edge set in place of a failure.

post.summary: Build a Lean package's HTML docs (doc-gen4)
post.description: Build the doc-gen4 HTML render of a folio's Lake package — the visualiser of a declared `lean` directory — with `lake -R -Kenv=dev build <Lib>:docs`, cache-aware: refuses while another lake/lean process holds `.lake/`, refuses on a restored tree that carries no traces (a Lake build there EVICTS the cache), checks or restores the warm cache first, and enables a sentinel-commented doc-gen4 `[[require]]` for this build only, restoring the lakefile on exit. Never runs `lake update`. Output: `<lake-root>/.lake/build/doc`.

lakeRoot.description: The Lake package directory whose lakefile requires (or sentinel-comments) doc-gen4, e.g. `folio/quantum-observable-universe/lean`.

lib.description: The `lean_lib` to document, e.g. `QOU` (a Lean library name: alphanumerics, dot, underscore, hyphen). Repeat for several.

restore.description: Restore the warm cache first (about 2 minutes) instead of only checking it.

allowCold.description: Build without a warm cache: Mathlib from source, 30-60 minutes before doc-gen4 starts.

dryRun.description: Run every guard, print the build command, build nothing.

render.description: `<lake-root>/.lake/build/doc`, doc-gen4's output, printed as the last line. Feed it to `lean-render-publish`.

x-selection.when: A folio's declared `lean` directory needs its visualiser (the doc-gen4 render) built or refreshed, before `lean-render-publish` wraps it.
x-selection.limits: doc-gen4 renders the WHOLE import closure, Mathlib included. It does not prune; prune at publish. Refuses, rather than risks, a shared or untraced `.lake/`. Never run it while another agent holds the folio's Lean cache.
x-selection.cost: Unmeasured. One doc-gen4 compile, then one doc pass per module of the closure — thousands for a Mathlib package; qou's July render was 4,193 pages, 545 MB. Needs that much free disk beyond the build.

post.summary: Publish the dynamic Lean viewer: doc-gen4 declaration data as knowledge-graph shards
post.description: Ingest doc-gen4's per-module declaration data (`.lake/build/doc-data/declaration-data-<Module>.bmp`) into JSON-LD shards — one per module, with declaration nodes, `imports` edges and `formalizes` edges to the content blocks whose `lean.ref` names each declaration — and publish them under the folio's site with a single viewer page that loads modules, signature chunks and the search list on demand. Signatures are chunked 500 declarations per file so a 12,804-declaration module stays usable. With `--base` it writes a STAGING overlay: only modules whose content hash differs from the published base, plus `overlay.json`; the viewer loads the rest from the base. Rails the viewer page with the same pass as `lean-render-publish`.

fromKg.description: An already-published combined KG (a viewer directory holding `data/`, e.g. the mounted Lean store, or its `data/`): cut this sub-KG out of it with no Lean build. Needs `--modules`.

sibling.description: `<package>/<Root>[,…]`: a link into module root `<Root>` goes to package `<package>`'s sub-KG, published beside this one (`../<package>/`). Repeat for several.

site.description: The folio's built site.

module.description: A module root to keep (`qou` keeps `QOU`). Repeat for several.

contentRoot.description: Content tree whose blocks' `lean.ref` become `formalizes` edges.

repo.description: `owner/repo` for block links.

ref.description: Branch or sha for block links.

contentPrefix.description: Path of the content root inside the repo, for block links.

base.description: Published `data/` of the base graph; enables the STAGING overlay.

externalBase.description: Where links into pruned modules go. Default the community mathlib4 docs.

facts.description: With `--json`: source path and sha256, page, page count, point geometry, pixel geometry, output bytes and sha256, media type, renderer version. Everything a provenance record needs and nothing it has to guess.

x-selection.when: A listing needs a cover and the bytes are already held. It renders page 1 by default and calls that the cover, because page 1 is a determined answer and "the cover" is not — the same choice `pdf-pages.py` makes about sections.
x-selection.limits: It decides nothing beyond the raster. WHICH documents get a cover, where the file lands, and what the catalogue must say about the derivation are the catalogue's to declare — see the content core's `scripts/gen-covers.ts`, which reads them from a layer's catalogue and refuses to write bytes for a THUMBNAIL that does not declare itself derived. It also cannot tell you whether the page it rendered IS the cover; it can only tell you it is page 1.
x-selection.cost: One PyMuPDF wheel, no network at run time, and a few milliseconds per page. Deterministic — identical input gives identical bytes, which is what lets a caller gate on `--check` rather than re-deciding.

post.summary: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs
post.description: Rewrite every third-party `uses: owner/repo@ref` outside the declared staging-only workflows to `@<full commit SHA> # <ref>`, so Dependabot keeps the pair current. A tag resolves to its PEELED commit (an annotated tag's object is never pinned), else a branch head, by `git ls-remote` with argv. A ref that resolves to nothing, or to more than one commit, is refused and reported, never guessed. This repository's own reusable workflows are first-party and left alone. Idempotent.

dry-run.description: Report what would be pinned and write nothing.

pinned.description: uses: lines pinned, per workflow, with every refused ref named; exit 1 when any is refused.

post.summary: Snapshot the SPDX License List at its pinned version
post.description: Read `json/licenses.json` and `json/exceptions.json` from a copy of github.com/spdx/license-list-data at the pinned tag and write `cat-harness/external-schemas/spdx-license-list.terminology.json` (`folio-pinned-terminology/v1`): every licence and exception id with its name and deprecated flag — the offline, version-fixed list `check:source-licence` validates a `licence.json` id against.

licenseListCheckout.description: A copy of github.com/spdx/license-list-data at tag `v<version>`, passed as `--from`. Named for what it is rather than `from`: with the same name it would share `pin-ig-terminology`'s signature and be DERIVED as its substitute, which it is not — an IG clone and a licence list are different inputs (`deriveAlternatives`). Refused unless both files declare the pin's `licenseListVersion`.

snapshot.description: `folio-pinned-terminology/v1`: the version, the source, and every `spdx-license#<id>` / `spdx-exception#<id>` with its name, sorted; `deprecated: true` where the List marks it.

x-selection.when: A licence id must be checked against a fixed, named edition of the SPDX License List rather than against whatever spdx.org serves today.
x-selection.limits: Ids, names and the deprecated flag only — not licence texts, URLs or OSI/FSF flags. The version comes from the pin record, never from this script; refreshing means moving the pin first.
x-selection.cost: Two JSON files (~380 KB) fetched once by hand; the ~105 KB snapshot is committed, so nothing runs at check time.

post.summary: Mount remote harnesses at a pinned commit, only when trusted
post.description: Lay down each declared remote mount — a `source.remote` layer in the root `index.config.json`, or, in a folio with no index, a `remoteMounts` entry on its declaration (both at once is refused) — and its dependency closure, from another repository at a full commit SHA. Write the lock, `index.lock.json` (a legacy `<name>.mount-lock.json` is read, and renamed onto it when rewritten), and, with an index, regenerate the root `.gitignore` block that ignores each mount path. It READS the declared mounts and never writes them: a tool that changes a mount writes through `writeDeclaredMounts` into `index.config.json`. Before anything is checked out, each mount must pass the trust gate (`schemas/kg/mount-trust.ts`, rule H8): a person's consent recorded for THIS pin, or a signature in a declared trust network. No signature verifier exists yet, so a signature alone is could-not-determine and does not mount. Unsigned and unconsented is refused. `--staging` mounts for a preview and needs neither. A directory id an override or `mountDefaults` names may be one the layer declares in its `<name>.json` or one it declares FROM WITHIN a declared directory (`skills/skills.json` naming `voices`), resolved at the pin through `instanceDirectories`; an id in neither is refused at plan time. `tools` on an override names Tools by id and mounts each one runnable: its definition (`<tools dir>/<id>/<id>.ts`), its implementation (the `inProcess.module`, or the script its `bun run cat <key>` resolves to) and their import closure, walked by bootstrap-tools' `importClosure` (the one closure walker), as every declared directory that closure touches — the lock still records directories only. A `hydrated` mount lays each chosen directory down as its published `index.hydrated.jsonld` only: read from the pin's git tree when a commit carries it, otherwise fetched from the pin's subgraph index package (the `subgraph-index-<sha>` release asset `subgraph-index-package` publishes), its tarball checked against its `folio-binary-release/v1` record, its manifest against the repository, pin and harness asked for, and each file against its sha256, `SubgraphHydratedSchema` and the subgraph IRI; the lock records the package's URL and sha256 so a replay fetches the same bytes. `--check` compares the disk against the lock and never fetches. When a run CHANGES the lock, it then re-renders the agent surface (`skill:commands` → `.claude/commands/`, `agent-memory` → `.claude/agent-memory/` and `.agents/`) from the checkout root, so a re-pin commit carries the skills and memory the new layers define; a generator that fails fails the run, and `--no-agent-surface` opts out.

check.description: Compare the disk against the lock; fetch nothing.

noAgentSurface.description: Do not re-render `.claude/commands/` and the agent memory after a mount that changed the lock.

noInstall.description: Lay the pinned bytes down without `bun install` in each mounted layer that carries a `package.json`. By default the install runs (`--production`; `--install-all` keeps devDependencies), so the mounted tools run; it writes only `node_modules/`, which no mount digest covers, so `--check` still passes.

seed.description: `<name>=<owner/repo>@<40-char sha>`: create or re-pin that remote layer in `index.config.json` instead of mounting, writing its `trust.consent` for that pin in the same write (needs `consentBy` and `evidence`; repeatable; `--whole` mounts every tracked file). Refused while a mount it moves has edits the lock does not hold, since the next mount would leave that mount at the old commit; `fresh` lets it through.

fresh.description: Replace a mount whose bytes no longer hash to the lock instead of leaving it untouched; with `seed`, re-pin over such edits. The edits are discarded.

choose.description: `<harness>[:<instance>]`: write a review's choice (`directories` and/or `tools`) into that mount entry's `overrides.<instance>` instead of mounting, so a fresh clone replays it. The pin and its consent are untouched; the next mount resolves the choice and the lock records what it resolved to.

directories.description: With `choose`: comma-separated directory ids, nested ids or concern names.

tools.description: With `choose`: comma-separated Tool ids, each mounted runnable.

evidence.description: With `seed`: where the consent was given, readable (a session, an issue comment), as `consent.evidence`. On stdin because it is free prose: it quotes what was said.

outcomes.description: Per layer: mounted, local, skipped, missing (including refused by the trust gate) or could-not-determine.

post.summary: Record what the publish branch served
post.description: Append one entry to the render log on the publish branch: what was published or taken down, when, from which commit, and — for a removal or a retention — WHY. The log is the only place a preview that vanished leaves a trace.

dir.description: A checkout of the publish branch, or a publish directory about to become one. This tool NEVER fetches, commits or pushes: the calling workflows hold the checkout with their own retry and concurrency handling, and a second pusher racing them could lose a deploy.

event.description: `rendered`, `removed`, `restored` or `retained`. `retained` records a removal CONSIDERED and refused, which would otherwise leave no trace.

kind.description: What was rendered — `staging-preview`, `site`, `export`. Open, not an enum: the publish branch carries more than previews, and an enum would make logging a new kind wait on a schema change.

path.description: The path on the publish branch. Checked as a VALUE, never trusted by provenance: the slug sanitiser can emit `..`, which is only safe for a slug taken from a git ref, and a dispatch input is not one.

slug.description: The staging slug, where the subject has one.

branch.description: The branch the render came from.

commit.description: The commit the artefact was built from.

run.description: The workflow run that wrote this, so a reader can open the log.

prose.description: One JSON object on STDIN: `{summary, reason?, detail?, format?}`. `summary` is required and one line. `reason` is required by the SCRIPT for `removed` and `retained`, because an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity the log exists to prevent. `format` declares how the prose reads (absent means plain text, never sniffed). Build it with `jq -n --arg`, never by concatenation.

entry.description: The day's JSONL the entry was APPENDED to. Append is the only verb: there is no `--remove`, no `--edit` and no `--id`, so a takedown is a `removed` ENTRY rather than the erasure of the `rendered` one before it, and the never-delete rule is structural rather than a guard every cleanup path must remember.

x-selection.when: Whenever something is published to or removed from the publish branch — including a removal that was refused. Called from `feature-staging.yml` at four points; `staging-render-log.bpmn` is the process.
x-selection.limits: It writes into a directory and does not push, so a caller that forgets to commit the log has written nothing durable. It cannot edit or delete an entry, by design. `--summary` / `--reason` / `--detail` are REFUSED as flags at exit 2 rather than ignored: they go on stdin, and a caller still passing them is told instead of silently logging an entry with no summary.
x-selection.cost: One appended line. No network.

post.summary: The render pipeline, in dependency order
post.description: Flatten the repository's renders into the order their `needs` imply, and optionally run them. Two stages: the current declared state as json/jsonld and the README derived from it are FATAL; the dynamic renderers (viewers, visualisers, doc pages, diagrams) skip and log; the dynamic-state export closes it. A cycle or a missing dependency yields NO order rather than a partial one.

dry_run.description: Print the flattened order and each step's failure policy without running anything.

report.description: Per step: ran, failed, skipped, or PENDING — declared with no implementation yet, which is never rendered as a pass.

post.summary: Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes
post.description: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled `no-sheet` and, with `--author`, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints `{"status":"unchanged"}` and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column `@login (#N): first paragraph`, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked `closed`), and `closedRows`, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled `change-set` unless `--label` says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an `issue-unlinked` change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With `--accept` it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against.

repo.description: The folio repository, `owner/name`, whose issues, open and closed, are read with `gh api`.

sheet.description: The Contributor Feedback tab's values (a public-comment log: Review Change Sets) as JSON: the Sheets API `values` array (or the whole `get_values` answer), from row 1, so the header row (first cell `Change-set`) is found.

state.description: The last check's state file. Missing on the first check, which reports every open issue as opened.

issues.description: Issues as JSON (the issues API's shape), instead of reading them with `gh api`. For tests and offline runs.

author.description: Only issues this GitHub login opened. Default every author.

sheetHash.description: The sheet script's hash of the person-set cells, Watch!G1. Given, it stands for the cells, so `--sheet` needs only the header row and the Issue column.

label.description: Only issues with this label, e.g. `change-set`. Default every issue on a read with an Issue column, and `change-set` on one without (a public-comment log).

skipLabel.description: The label that keeps an issue off the sheet. Default `no-sheet`.

result.description: JSON on standard output: `status` (`unchanged` or `changed`), `digest`, and when changed `changes`, `append` (rows aligned to the header, each with `closed`), `closedRows` and `state`. Exit 0 unchanged, 10 changed, 2 usage.

x-selection.when: On every poll of a review-log watcher, before any agent work: the agent pass runs only when this reports `changed`.
x-selection.limits: Reads one tab and one repository's issues; it never writes the sheet or GitHub. It sees an edit only in the watched headers, so the agent's own Green columns and the script's Grey ones never wake the watcher.
x-selection.cost: One `gh api` call per 100 issues and one small JSON file; well under a second.

post.summary: Build the review sheet's Apps Script and a document's Config tab
post.description: Builds `Code.gs` (`--script`), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from `review-sheet.gs`), and one document's Config tab rows (`--config`), filled from the folio's `review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json`, its review anchors and the draft's `pdf-line-map.json`. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet's links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each `No. n` linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document's URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet's Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs `installTriggers`; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With `"mode": "drafting"` in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document's table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab.

repo.description: The folio repository. Default the current directory.

config.description: The folio's sheet settings, e.g. `review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json`: anchors, lineMap, draftUrl, commentUrl, and optional namedSections, aliases, tabs and columns. A drafting sheet's config (`review/drafting/sheet-sync.json`) has mode `drafting`, anchors and sectionUrl.

out.description: Where to write the Config tab's rows (JSON). Default standard output.

script.description: Code.gs, ready to paste into any review sheet's Apps Script editor. Never committed: it is rebuilt from the template.

configRows.description: The Config tab's rows for one document, which the agent writes into the sheet. Never committed: rebuilt from the config.

x-install.service: Google Apps Script bound to the review sheet: copy the template, have the agent write its Config tab, add editors to the "Ready columns: editors" lock, paste Code.gs, run installTriggers (skill review-sheet-script, "Setting up a sheet for a new document")

Findings: used-not-declared, declared-not-used, declared-not-present, present-not-declared (reported, never deleted), naming advisories, and expiry (≤30 days minor, ≤7 major, expired critical). Exits 2 when anything could not be determined, which outranks clean; else 1 on a major or critical finding; else 0.

Every check is reported as pass, fail or unknown; a blocking check that fails OR could not be run refuses the release, because could-not-check is never clean. Advisories are reported and never block. Called by `prepare-merge` before a push that will merge, and by any publish process before it publishes.
