post.summary: Is this repository's cutover from the monorepo complete? Measured, condition by condition
post.description: Run in a separated repository. Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate: `mounts` (every declared layer on disk at its pin — `remote-mount --check`), `declarations` (every path a declaration names resolves — `declaration-resolution`), `monorepo-paths` (no wiring still names the monorepo: `livesAt` on it, a submodule of it, a reusable workflow called from it, a path into its old checkout — the one condition implemented here), `import-direction` and `reference-direction` (no layer reaches a layer above it), and `site` (the site builds from the mounts alone, every link resolving — `build-instance-site --no-mount`, only with `--site`). Findings inside a MOUNTED layer are listed and not counted: a defect in a layer pinned from upstream is fixed upstream and re-pinned. Exit 0 complete, 1 a condition failed, 2 a condition could not be determined or was not run — without `--site` the answer is never 0.

post.summary: Publish a folio's or an IG's site from the agent's own checkout — the one agent publish path
post.description: Build a repository's site in the agent's checkout and push it to the publish branch, as a preview or as the main site, without an Actions runner. Which build is read from the repository: a declared `site.build` recipe (built by `build-instance-site`), else the reusable workflow its own workflow files call — `folio-staging.yml` for a folio, the WHO SMART Base IG's `ghbuild.yml` for a FHIR IG, whose `build` job is planned step by step and run as written. For an IG it then applies the harness chrome over the built output (`sync-docs-harness`, then `rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site --instance <the IG>`): every page gains the rail and the icon row `#fa-navbar-row`, and the IG's own content is left byte for byte. A root publish is REFUSED when the chrome cannot be applied, and a clean root deploy is refused over any root whose `index.html` wears the icon row unless the new output does too, so a chromed root is never replaced by bare IG Publisher pages. Every run prints its plan first, and the plan lists the chrome step; `--plan` stops there, `--dry-run` composes the commit in a temporary worktree and pushes nothing, `--artifact` writes a claude.ai Artifact bundle instead.

Without a `site.build` recipe an IG falls back to its own workflow's Publisher steps, which need a Docker daemon and give the rail and icon row only.

post.summary: Collect candidate translations from open engines
post.description: Ask one or more open, self-hosted machine translators — OPUS-MT (Helsinki-NLP Marian models, CC-BY 4.0, run locally) and/or a self-hosted LibreTranslate (AGPL, Argos models) — for CANDIDATE translations of each empty or fuzzy string, so no freemium API quota is involved. Candidates are appended to `<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json` (`translation-candidates/v1`) for a reviewer to choose among on the translation review page; a candidate whose placeholders or markup do not round-trip is not recorded. Candidates are never a barrier to having a translation: an EMPTY msgstr gets the first good candidate, marked `#, fuzzy`; a non-empty msgstr is never overwritten. The translation node records the source (`generatedBy: "machine"`, model, time); `official` is never set, and a candidate is never a verdict. A catalogue that says DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, or whose node is official, gets candidates but no fill.

engines.description: Comma-separated candidate sources, tried in this order for an empty msgstr: `opus-mt` (the local runner `scripts/translation/opus_mt_runner.py`, shared with `translate-pot`, which needs the extended Python tier) and/or `libretranslate` (the URL below). Absent, the command exits 2.

url.description: A self-hosted LibreTranslate's base URL (default `http://localhost:5000`). The hosted libretranslate.com / .de services are refused.

locales.description: Comma-separated locales to fill, e.g. `es,fr`. Default: every locale directory except the source locale.

init.description: Start a `.po` from each template that has none (locale named, `X-Folio-Official: no`, every msgstr empty), then collect candidates for it. Never the default: starting a catalogue is a decision.

candidates.description: `translations/<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json` (`translation-candidates/v1`), appended to: each candidate carries its text and source `{kind: "open-mt", id: <model>, version?, at}`. Identical text from the same source is not added twice.

x-selection.when: A catalogue has empty or fuzzy entries and machine drafts are wanted for a reviewer to choose among on the translation review page. Every candidate is a draft; a person's adjudication decides.
x-selection.limits: Singular entries only: plural entries are left for a person. Catalogues that say DO NOT MACHINE-FILL, and catalogues whose node is official, are refused. Machine output into a language nobody on the project reads cannot be checked here; it is a draft for review, never a sign-off. The LibreTranslate host is whatever `--url` names (normally one on this machine), so it has no fixed remedy; without one, use `--engine opus-mt`.
x-selection.cost: OPUS-MT: a model download per language pair on first use (hundreds of MB) and CPU time, no per-string fee. LibreTranslate: whatever running your own instance costs.

post.summary: Where to drop a file — the queue's upload URL
post.description: Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the layer's own declaration: the `uploads` graph's directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub's `/upload/<branch>/<path>`. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared `uploads` graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no `origin` remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. The declared path is relative to the LAYER and a forge URL needs it relative to the REPOSITORY, so pasting the declared path can mint a 404.

branch.description: The branch the upload form targets. Defaults to `main`; pass the working branch to send somebody to a pull request's head instead, so the upload lands on a commit CI judges.

url.description: The upload URL on stdout, exit 0 — or, on stderr and exit 1, the reason it could not be composed and the remedy for that reason. Never a guessed URL: a URL is believed, and somebody sent to a wrong one cannot tell it from an empty directory.

x-selection.when: You are about to tell somebody where to put a file, in any channel. Reach for it every time, not only when unsure: a hand-written path breaks silently when a directory moves. It also answers "which queue" when a checkout declares more than one (one per layer): the answer is whichever layer root you pass, never a literal.
x-selection.limits: It answers WHERE, and nothing else. It does not upload, does not check whether the person has write access, and cannot tell you which of several declared queues should own a given file — that is undecided and `upload-routes` says so rather than picking. The `/upload/<branch>/<path>` form is GitHub's, so another forge gets a named refusal rather than a guess. And the URL it hands back opens the route with the FEWEST guarantees: the web form has no working tree, so no pre-commit hook and no generator run happen on it, and everything `upload-routes` lists has to be discharged afterwards from a checkout.
x-selection.cost: One read of the declaration and one of the git remote; no network at run time and nothing installed.

A table is shaped like a FHIR ConceptMap: an existing ConceptMap, R4 or R5, is representable as one without loss (`fromConceptMap`), and a table can be produced as a ConceptMap (`toConceptMap`), which returns every loss rather than dropping anything silently. post.summary: Wireframe check at web and mobile viewports
post.description: Render each mid-fidelity wireframe candidate of one topic at a web viewport (1280x800) and a mobile viewport (390x844). For each viewport it records `script` entries for renders, no-overflow and no-placeholder, each pass or fail with a note. It writes a screenshot per viewport and a report.json carrying the use, topic and surface, and exits 1 on any fail and 2 when the candidate set is not one the use admits.

use.description: `design` or `as-is`. Design needs at least two candidates, compared blind; as-is candidates are drawings of what renders on main, each marked `as-is` in its file name. Anything else exits 2.

topic.description: Which wireframe is checked: its asset directory, docs/wireframes/<topic>/ for as-is use and docs/proposals/<topic>/wireframes/ for design use (docs/wireframes/<topic>/ is also accepted there). With no candidates, every .html in it is checked; a candidate outside it is refused.

surface.description: What is drawn: a visualiser route key or a chrome name. Recorded in report.json; for as-is use it must be the topic itself or a ref docs/wireframes/index.json says the topic covers.

candidates.description: Wireframe HTML files, all in the topic's directory. Absent: every .html there. Each must carry both a web and a mobile layout (responsive CSS or two layouts).

out.description: Where screenshots and report.json go; default <the topic's directory>/checks.

report.description: report.json: per candidate, per viewport, per criterion. The screenshots are beside it.

post.description: Check every `*.witness.json` in the folio's declared `computation-witness` directories against the two schemas in `schemas/computation-witness.ts`: the envelope every witness should meet (a failure is a malformed file) and the producer contract (a failure is a finding against the producer, grouped by the fields at fault). Also lists files that are not strict JSON, which Python's reader accepts and every other consumer rejects. Report-only: it never edits a witness, which is generator output.

dir.description: Check this directory instead of the declared ones, e.g. before a folio declares the kind.

json.description: Machine-readable output, every finding group listed.

strict.description: Exit 1 when any witness is malformed or not strict JSON. Contract findings never fail the run.

report.description: Counts of witnesses, malformed files, non-strict-JSON files and contract conformance, then the contract findings by field. Exit 2 when no directory declares the kind and no `--dir` was given: a clean report over nothing is not a pass.

post.description: List the content-wired computation scripts a witness refresh would run, without running any of them or writing a witness.
